title: decode() accepts hashids produced with a different salt
body:
In `hashids.py`, `Hashids.decode` is supposed to return an empty tuple
for anything that is not a valid hashid for this instance's salt,
alphabet and minimum length. It currently returns whatever numbers the
characters happen to map to:

```python
>>> Hashids("salt A").decode(Hashids("salt B").encode(5))
(some unrelated numbers)   # expected ()
```

We use the salt to keep ids from different tables apart, so this lets
an id of one table resolve to a row of another. A string must decode
to numbers only if encoding those numbers gives back exactly the same
string; otherwise `decode` must return `()`.
provenance: upstream code at a pinned commit with an injected regression; the oracle is the unmodified upstream file
